chunk_findings.detail: The added table and comment claim to stop machine-local writes, including “reviewers and endpoints”, from going to the committed layer, but the table contains only four `schedule.*` parallelism keys. For an endpoint/reviewer key not listed here, `machine_local_layer()` returns `""`, so a command such as `ddflow config reviewers alice` with no `--local` still targets `.ddflow/config.toml`, the committed layer. That is the same mislayering the change says it is fixing, but only the schedule/parallelism keys are actually fixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/configwrite.py:MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS

chunk_findings.detail: `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS` is declared as `dict[str, str]` and is described as a classification with a default layer per key, but `machine_local_layer()` ignores the values entirely and only tests key membership. It always returns `"local"` for any key in the table, regardless of the value associated with that key. For example, if the table is extended with a key mapped to `""` to mean “write to the committed layer”, `machine_local_layer(set(), that_key)` still returns `"local"`, contradicting the stated per-key default-layer design.

chunk_findings.detail: The knob test does not establish that `enforce.machine_local_keys` caused the local write. It discards the result of `run_cli(repo, "config", "--set", "enforce.machine_local_keys", '["lease.ttl_s"]')` on line 43, so a failed knob write is silent; it never checks that `lease.ttl_s` defaults to the committed layer before the knob is set; and it never checks that a shipped machine-local key remains local after the knob is set. If the implementation ignores the knob but `lease.ttl_s` is already machine-local, if unknown keys default to local, or if the knob replaces the shipped classification instead of extending it, this test still passes, so it does not verify the promised “extends the classification”.

chunk_findings.detail:
For `append_toml`, `_default_layer` selects a single layer for the entire TOML payload based on whether the payload’s top-level table set is considered machine-local. A payload that mixes machine-local and non-machine-local tables is therefore routed wholly to one layer. For example, given `edit.append_toml = '[project]
name = "x"
[reviewers]
name = "a"
'`, `tables` contains `{"project", "reviewers"}`; because `reviewers` is machine-local, `machine_local_tables` returns true, `_default_layer` returns `"local"`, and `configure` writes the whole document—including the non-machine-local `[project]` keys—to `.ddflow/local/config.toml`. The docstring says reviewer/companion-only documents default local, but the code does not enforce that restriction or split mixed payloads, so committed-layer keys can be silently mislayered local.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py:_default_layer

chunk_findings.detail: `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS` is documented as a table of machine-local keys and “the layer their writes default to”, and its type is `dict[str, str]`, but `machine_local_layer()` (and `machine_local_tables()`) never read the mapping values; they only test membership in the key set. Thus the code cannot honor a stated default layer other than `"local"`: if the table is extended as its type/comment permit with an entry such as `"schedule.parallel": ""` to mean “write this key to the committed layer”, `machine_local_layer(set(), "schedule.parallel")` still returns `"local"`, and `machine_local_tables(set(), {"schedule.parallel"})` still returns `True`. The earlier triage probe (“separator-agnostic path assert”) does not answer this because it does not change the value-ignoring logic.

chunk_findings.detail:
For `append_toml`, `_default_layer` still selects a single layer for the entire TOML payload: it parses the document into its top-level key/table names, asks `CW.machine_local_tables(...)` once, and `configure` then passes the resulting single `local` flag to `CW.write_append`. Given a payload that mixes machine-local and shared tables, e.g. `edit.append_toml = '[reviewers]
name = "alice"
[project]
name = "x"
'`, the code cannot route `[reviewers]` to the local layer while routing `[project]` to the committed layer. If `machine_local_tables` returns true for any machine-local table, `[project]` is silently written to the local layer; if it returns true only when all tables are machine-local, `[reviewers]` is silently written to the committed layer. Either way, some machine-local or shared data is written to the wrong layer, and the diff does not add per-table routing, splitting, or rejection of mixed payloads, so the previous finding is not answered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py:_default_layer

chunk_findings.detail: The validation regex allows only a single dot, so it rejects legitimate dotted keys with three or more segments even though the comment describes plain keys as “dot-separated segments.” For example, setting `[enforce].machine_local_keys = ["lease.ttl_s.enabled"]` causes `_extra_machine_local_problem` to return a refusal because `_PLAIN_DOTTED.fullmatch("lease.ttl_s.enabled")` fails, even though that value is a dotted config key under the documented CLI key form and cannot be added to the machine-local classification.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/enforce.py:_PLAIN_DOTTED

chunk_findings.detail:
The new `machine_local_tables` helper is all-or-nothing: it returns true only when *every* top-level table name in the appended TOML payload is already classified as machine-local. If `_default_layer` uses this boolean to choose the destination for the whole `append_toml` payload, a mixed payload is routed entirely to one layer. For example, `edit.append_toml = '[[reviewer]]
name = "a"
[project]
name = "x"
'` produces table names `{"reviewer", "project"}`. `machine_local_tables(extra, {"reviewer", "project"})` is false because `project` is not machine-local, so the whole payload defaults to the committed layer and the machine-local `[[reviewer]]` block is written to `.ddflow/config.toml`. This is the same leak the change is meant to prevent; the new helper does not split the payload or classify each table/key independently, so the earlier mixed-payload finding still holds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py:_default_layer (via configwrite.machine_local_tables)

chunk_findings.detail: `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS` is documented and typed as a mapping from a key to “the layer their writes default to,” but the helpers never read the mapping values. `machine_local_layer` returns hardcoded `"local"` for any membership, and `machine_local_tables` treats any key present in `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS` as machine-local regardless of its value. Thus if the table is extended in the way its type/comment permit with a committed-layer entry, e.g. `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS["schedule.parallel"] = ""`, `machine_local_layer({}, "schedule.parallel")` still returns `"local"` instead of `""`. The stated per-key default layer is not actually honored.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/configwrite.py:machine_local_layer

chunk_findings.detail: The knob test still does not establish that `[enforce].machine_local_keys` *extends* the shipped classification. It only checks that `lease.ttl_s` was not written to the committed file after the knob is set; it ignores the command result, never asserts that `lease.ttl_s` defaulted to the committed layer before the knob was set, and never asserts that a shipped machine-local key still defaults to the local layer after the knob is set. If a future change made the knob replace the shipped set (or if `_extra_keys` accidentally did), `schedule.parallel` would stop defaulting local and this test would still pass. The diff does not add those missing assertions, so the previous finding remains.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_machine_local_keys.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: This test still does not establish that `[enforce].machine_local_keys` *extends* the shipped machine-local classification. It ignores the result of `config --set enforce.machine_local_keys ...`, never checks that `lease.ttl_s` defaults to the committed layer before the knob is set, and never checks a shipped machine-local key after the knob is set. If the `--set` call fails but `lease.ttl_s` is already machine-local, or if the implementation treats the knob as a replacement for the shipped key set, the test still passes: `lease.ttl_s` may be written to the local layer while a shipped key such as `schedule.max_parallel_tasks` is incorrectly written to the committed layer. That passes the test while violating the intended “knob extends the classification” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_machine_local_keys.py:test_the_enforce_knob_extends_classification

chunk_findings.detail:
`_default_layer` chooses the local layer for an appended TOML document if *any* top-level table is machine-local, rather than only when the document is entirely machine-local/reviewer/companion. Given `edit.append_toml = '[reviewers]
alice = "x"
[enforce]
machine_local_keys = ["lease.ttl_s"]'`, `tomllib.loads` yields top-level tables `{"reviewers", "enforce"}`; `CW.machine_local_tables(...)` returns true because `reviewers` is machine-local, so `_default_layer` returns `"local"`. `configure` then sets `target` to `.ddflow/local/config.toml` and passes `local=True` to the append, writing the non-machine-local `[enforce]` knob to the local layer even though the change promises only machine-local writes default to local. The docstring says reviewer/companion-only documents default local, but the implementation does not require all top-level tables to be machine-local.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py:_default_layer

chunk_findings.detail: The validator is narrower than the documented key form. The comment describes a key as “dot-separated segments,” but the pattern `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` used with `fullmatch` permits exactly one dot. Thus a dotted key with a nested segment, e.g. `["acp.providers.claude.model"]` or `["lease.ttl_s.foo"]`, is rejected with “is not a dotted config key” even though it is a dotted key; the knob cannot extend the machine-local classification for any valid multi-segment dotted key. The message also misdescribes `a.b.c` as not dotted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/enforce.py:_PLAIN_DOTTED

chunk_findings.detail: The table is declared as `dict[str, str]` and documented as mapping each key to “the layer their writes default to”, but `machine_local_layer()` ignores the values entirely and hard-codes `"local"` for any key whose exact name or first dotted segment is present. `machine_local_tables()` similarly uses only the key set. Therefore the stated per-key layer is not honored: if the table is extended as its type and comment invite, e.g. with an entry whose value is `""` to mean “default to the committed layer”, `machine_local_layer(set(), "that.key")` still returns `"local"` because membership succeeds. The earlier triage note “fixed: path asserted separator-agnostic” does not address this; the code still never reads `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS` values.

chunk_findings.detail: The test named “extends the classification” does not actually test extension. It sets `enforce.machine_local_keys` without checking the result of that `config --set`, then only writes `lease.ttl_s` and checks that that key lands local while the committed file stays clean. It never checks that a shipped machine-local key such as `schedule.max_parallel_tasks` remains local after the knob is present. Thus a regression where `enforce.machine_local_keys` replaces the shipped table instead of extending it would still pass: set the knob to `["lease.ttl_s"]`, make `machine_local_layer()` use only the knob when non-empty, then `lease.ttl_s` writes local and the committed file is clean, so lines 49–51 pass, while `schedule.max_parallel_tasks` has wrongly regressed to the committed layer. The earlier “committed file stays clean” assertion does not answer this, because it only proves the newly classified key did not go committed; it does not prove the knob extended the shipped classification or that existing machine-local keys survived.

chunk_findings.detail:
For `append_toml`, `_default_layer` still selects a single layer for the entire TOML payload: it parses the document into its top-level key/table names, asks `CW.machine_local_tables(...)` once, and `configure` then passes the resulting single `local` flag to `CW.write_append`. Given a payload that mixes machine-local and shared tables, e.g. `edit.append_toml = '[reviewers]
name = "alice"
[project]
name = "x"
'`, the code cannot route `[reviewers]` to the local layer while routing `[project]` to the committed layer. If `machine_local_tables` returns true for any machine-local table, `[project]` is silently written to the local layer; if it returns true only when all tables are machine-local, `[reviewers]` is silently written to the committed layer. Either way, some machine-local or shared data is written to the wrong layer, and the diff does not add per-table routing, splitting, or rejection of mixed payloads, so the previous finding is not answered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py:_default_layer

chunk_findings.detail: The validation regex allows only a single dot, so it rejects legitimate dotted keys with three or more segments even though the comment describes plain keys as “dot-separated segments.” For example, setting `[enforce].machine_local_keys = ["lease.ttl_s.enabled"]` causes `_extra_machine_local_problem` to return a refusal because `_PLAIN_DOTTED.fullmatch("lease.ttl_s.enabled")` fails, even though that value is a dotted config key under the documented CLI key form and cannot be added to the machine-local classification.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/enforce.py:_PLAIN_DOTTED

chunk_findings.detail:
The new `machine_local_tables` helper is all-or-nothing: it returns true only when *every* top-level table name in the appended TOML payload is already classified as machine-local. If `_default_layer` uses this boolean to choose the destination for the whole `append_toml` payload, a mixed payload is routed entirely to one layer. For example, `edit.append_toml = '[[reviewer]]
name = "a"
[project]
name = "x"
'` produces table names `{"reviewer", "project"}`. `machine_local_tables(extra, {"reviewer", "project"})` is false because `project` is not machine-local, so the whole payload defaults to the committed layer and the machine-local `[[reviewer]]` block is written to `.ddflow/config.toml`. This is the same leak the change is meant to prevent; the new helper does not split the payload or classify each table/key independently, so the earlier mixed-payload finding still holds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py:_default_layer (via configwrite.machine_local_tables)

chunk_findings.detail: `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS` is documented and typed as a mapping from a key to “the layer their writes default to,” but the helpers never read the mapping values. `machine_local_layer` returns hardcoded `"local"` for any membership, and `machine_local_tables` treats any key present in `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS` as machine-local regardless of its value. Thus if the table is extended in the way its type/comment permit with a committed-layer entry, e.g. `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS["schedule.parallel"] = ""`, `machine_local_layer({}, "schedule.parallel")` still returns `"local"` instead of `""`. The stated per-key default layer is not actually honored.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/configwrite.py:machine_local_layer

chunk_findings.detail: The knob test still does not establish that `[enforce].machine_local_keys` *extends* the shipped classification. It only checks that `lease.ttl_s` was not written to the committed file after the knob is set; it ignores the command result, never asserts that `lease.ttl_s` defaulted to the committed layer before the knob was set, and never asserts that a shipped machine-local key still defaults to the local layer after the knob is set. If a future change made the knob replace the shipped set (or if `_extra_keys` accidentally did), `schedule.parallel` would stop defaulting local and this test would still pass. The diff does not add those missing assertions, so the previous finding remains.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_machine_local_keys.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: This test still does not establish that `[enforce].machine_local_keys` *extends* the shipped machine-local classification. It ignores the result of `config --set enforce.machine_local_keys ...`, never checks that `lease.ttl_s` defaults to the committed layer before the knob is set, and never checks a shipped machine-local key after the knob is set. If the `--set` call fails but `lease.ttl_s` is already machine-local, or if the implementation treats the knob as a replacement for the shipped key set, the test still passes: `lease.ttl_s` may be written to the local layer while a shipped key such as `schedule.max_parallel_tasks` is incorrectly written to the committed layer. That passes the test while violating the intended “knob extends the classification” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_machine_local_keys.py:test_the_enforce_knob_extends_classification

chunk_findings.detail: The new lookup order gives `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS` absolute precedence over `[enforce].machine_local_keys`, so a more specific extra classification can be shadowed by a table-level mapping entry. With a committed-layer table entry such as `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS = {"lease": ""}` (allowed by the new “value is the layer” contract) and `extra = {"lease.ttl_s"}` from `enforce.machine_local_keys=["lease.ttl_s"]`, `machine_local_layer(extra, "lease.ttl_s")` skips the exact `extra` check and returns `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS["lease"]`, i.e. `""`, so `ddflow config lease.ttl_s 100` writes the committed layer despite the knob. The previous code checked `dotted in extra` before the head lookup, so this is a regression in the knob’s extension semantics.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/configwrite.py:machine_local_layer

chunk_findings.detail: The added assertions only establish that `lease.ttl_s` changes from committed to local after the knob is set; they still do not establish that the knob *extends* the shipped classification rather than replacing it. No assertion after setting `enforce.machine_local_keys` checks that a shipped machine-local key still defaults to the local layer. If `machine_local_layer` were changed to ignore `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS` whenever `extra` is non-empty, this test would still pass, so it does not verify the intended extension behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_machine_local_keys.py:test_the_enforce_knob_extends_the_classification

chunk_findings.detail:
For `append_toml`, `_default_layer` still selects a single layer for the entire TOML payload: it parses the document into its top-level key/table names, asks `CW.machine_local_tables(...)` once, and `configure` then passes the resulting single `local` flag to `CW.write_append`. Given a payload that mixes machine-local and shared tables, e.g. `edit.append_toml = '[reviewers]
name = "alice"
[project]
name = "x"
'`, the code cannot route `[reviewers]` to the local layer while routing `[project]` to the committed layer. If `machine_local_tables` returns true for any machine-local table, `[project]` is silently written to the local layer; if it returns true only when all tables are machine-local, `[reviewers]` is silently written to the committed layer. Either way, some machine-local or shared data is written to the wrong layer, and the diff does not add per-table routing, splitting, or rejection of mixed payloads, so the previous finding is not answered.

chunk_findings.detail: The validation regex allows only a single dot, so it rejects legitimate dotted keys with three or more segments even though the comment describes plain keys as “dot-separated segments.” For example, setting `[enforce].machine_local_keys = ["lease.ttl_s.enabled"]` causes `_extra_machine_local_problem` to return a refusal because `_PLAIN_DOTTED.fullmatch("lease.ttl_s.enabled")` fails, even though that value is a dotted config key under the documented CLI key form and cannot be added to the machine-local classification.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/enforce.py:_PLAIN_DOTTED

chunk_findings.detail:
The new `machine_local_tables` helper is all-or-nothing: it returns true only when *every* top-level table name in the appended TOML payload is already classified as machine-local. If `_default_layer` uses this boolean to choose the destination for the whole `append_toml` payload, a mixed payload is routed entirely to one layer. For example, `edit.append_toml = '[[reviewer]]
name = "a"
[project]
name = "x"
'` produces table names `{"reviewer", "project"}`. `machine_local_tables(extra, {"reviewer", "project"})` is false because `project` is not machine-local, so the whole payload defaults to the committed layer and the machine-local `[[reviewer]]` block is written to `.ddflow/config.toml`. This is the same leak the change is meant to prevent; the new helper does not split the payload or classify each table/key independently, so the earlier mixed-payload finding still holds.

chunk_findings.detail: `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS` is documented and typed as a mapping from a key to “the layer their writes default to,” but the helpers never read the mapping values. `machine_local_layer` returns hardcoded `"local"` for any membership, and `machine_local_tables` treats any key present in `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS` as machine-local regardless of its value. Thus if the table is extended in the way its type/comment permit with a committed-layer entry, e.g. `MACHINE_LOCAL_KEYS["schedule.parallel"] = ""`, `machine_local_layer({}, "schedule.parallel")` still returns `"local"` instead of `""`. The stated per-key default layer is not actually honored.
